# RustyNES v3.5.1 — "Reprise"

A patch release on v3.5.0 "Chorus": the MMC5 applies its split-screen and extended-attribute CHR banks only while the PPU renders, in both cores, and the suggestions left open in v3.5.0's review are settled. **Movies and netplay peers from v3.5.0 are refused** (emulation epoch 7; v3.5.0 recorded 6), with a message naming both epochs; save states from v3.5.0 load, and netplay protocol 9 and `.rnm` format 7 are unchanged.

## Fixed

- **MMC5 CHR reads outside rendering.** The MMC5 latches a CHR bank for each background tile it substitutes: the split region's `$5202` bank, and in extended-attribute mode a 4 KiB bank per tile. RustyNES kept applying the last tile's bank after the frame ended, so a `$2007` read of CHR in vertical blank, or with rendering switched off, read that tile's bank instead of the bank registers. The NESdev MMC5 page describes both as substitutions made to background fetches while the PPU renders, and gives `$2007` "the last set of registers written to"; it also names the games that read CHR this way, Bandit Kings of Ancient China and Uchuu Keibitai SDF, and the Koei games keep extended attributes on throughout. Both overrides now apply only to a fetch made while rendering. The MiSTer core had the same defect, and one more instance of it: a `$2007` read of the nametable in vertical blank after a split frame returned the split's data. Both are fixed there.
- **A key held while it is rebound is released.** Rebinding a controller, Power Pad, Hyper Shot, microphone or Family BASIC key while it was held left that input pressed until the app restarted, because the key's release no longer matched the position its press had set. A rebind now releases every keyboard-held input; press the key again to hold it.
- **Opening a device or a pipe no longer hangs the desktop app.** Every file the app opens at your request (ROMs, patches, the FDS BIOS, movies, TAStudio projects, symbol files, source maps, Lua scripts, palettes, splits files and the per-game file beside a ROM) was read whole with no limit, so a named pipe blocked the window thread and a device such as `/dev/zero` filled memory. Anything that is not a regular file is now refused, and files are read up to 64 MiB. `rustynes verify` and `rustynes speedrun` read their inputs the same way.

## What the MMC5 fix changes in recorded play

- No snapshot or fingerprint moved: the local commercial suites (60 real games, Castlevania III, Bandit Kings and Uchuu Keibitai SDF among them; 169 extended; 6 coverage) and the epoch fingerprint pass unchanged.
- A temporary probe counted every CHR access where the old behaviour would have chosen a different bank, over 3,600 frames of each of those three games with their menus driven: none.
- **The emulation epoch rises to 7 anyway** (maintainer). The fix changes what a `$2007` CHR read in vertical blank returns, and a v3.5.0 movie of a game that makes that read (a Koei screen after an extended-attribute frame, say) would replay differently with no warning. With the epoch raised, such a movie is refused with the reason instead. Re-record v3.5.0 movies under v3.5.1, and keep both netplay peers on the same release.

## Settled from the v3.5.0 review

- **`lua_eval` from the MCP server during a real-time run is safe.** Each running frame and each tool call take the same lock, so an evaluation sees one frame boundary and the runner waits for it. A test now evaluates Lua mid-run and checks that the run's recording still replays.
- **The Windows shared-memory tests run in CI**, along with the macOS ones (added in the v3.5.0 post-release work, `T-WIN-SCRIPT-IPC-CI`). Their first run passed on Windows, including the region-grow recovery test, and found a macOS-only fault in one test's setup, which was fixed.
- **MiSTer:** a register that fed nothing was removed. The nametable-override and IRQ outputs are not gated by the board select, but the registers that drive them can only be written while the MMC5 is the loaded board, so no other board can see them; the reasoning is recorded beside the code.

## The MiSTer core

- The MMC5 fix is in the RTL, with a new stimulus that reads CHR and the nametable through `$2007` in vertical blank after a split frame and an extended-attribute frame; its goldens come from the fixed oracle, and the pin moves to this release.
- **New bitstreams** are compiled from the sibling's release commit at release time and attached here and to the sibling's release; their seed, checksums and timing margins are in its v3.5.1 notes.
- **Release candidate, not hardware-verified.** No hardware has run any bitstream.

## Verification

- The MMC5 rule: a failing unit test for each latch first, then passing; five existing tests that made background fetches without rendering on now set it, which is what they model.
- The rebind fix and the file reader: each change made to fail by a mutation that undoes it.
- `rustynes-mappers` 1,113 passed; `rustynes-frontend` 780 passed, 1 ignored; the MCP server's tests pass; clippy clean for the workspace, every frontend feature set and both WebAssembly builds; the API docs build without warnings; the `no_std` core builds.
- The release audits (anchors, state prose, notes rendering, the libretro `.info`, the contribution checklist) pass on the bumped tree.

## Install

- Download the pre-built binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows below.
- The MiSTer bitstreams are attached below as a release candidate, not hardware-verified: `RustyNES_MiSTer-v3.5.1.rbf` (off-die, needs SDRAM) and `RustyNES_MiSTer-v3.5.1-lite.rbf` (on-die).
- The WebAssembly build is live at [doublegate.github.io/RustyNES](https://doublegate.github.io/RustyNES/).
- The RetroArch core is in RetroArch's Online Updater on the platforms the libretro buildbot publishes to.
